messages.author: 2300d3769456dbe6
messages.subject: Howto compile advanced models?
parts:
Dear members  of the Stan user list mailing group,

I am quite new to Stan, but have worked a lot with JAGS and WinBUGS. I recently wrote a multilevel (hierarchical) model with repeated measurements that I want to fit in RStan. This model compiles and runs fine when I have a dataset of limited size, but no longer compiles when I use the full dataset. I have a feeling this has something to do with the large amount of missing values: in the larger dataset (about 3000 subjects) I have studies with observations for only one (of the 6) follow-up time points. 

Following the instructions of the OpenBUGS example "camel" , I need to specify a parameter for each missing value in the " parameters section" . Since I am not interested in the actual values of the missing values, I am wondering more efficient ways exist to model the missing values. The current setup leads to a huge amout of parameters being estimated and stored in memory, this is not really what I want. 

In any case, the model that currently needs to be compiled uses about 41GB of RAM at the time it is aborted. This does not seem right. When I compile the same model with a smaller version of the dataset (only smaller in terms of #subjects, i.e. a total of +-300 subjects out of the +-3000 subjects), it compiles and runs perfectly, and requires about 1GB to 2GB of RAM. The smaller version has about 100 missing values.

Thanks in advance for your help!!

Thomas

>
> Following the instructions of the OpenBUGS example "camel" , I need to specify a parameter for each missing value in the " parameters section" . Since I am not interested in the actual values of the missing values, I am wondering more efficient ways exist to model the missing values.

The only other thing you can do is marginalize out the variable.

It's hard to say how to do that exactly without seeing more of your
model.

> The current setup leads to a huge amout of parameters being estimated and stored in memory, this is not really what I want.
>
> In any case, the model that currently needs to be compiled uses about 41GB of RAM at the time it is aborted.

Which version of RStan are you using?

The size Stan needs is based on the expression graph computed by
the model block. Stan consumes roughly 24 bytes per subexpression plus
8 bytes per operand.

A rough estimate should be about 40 bytes times the number of parameters,
assuming most of the operations are binary. The density functions are pretty
economical --- they take 16 bytes per operand but only form a single expression.

> This does not seem right. When I compile the same model with a smaller version of the dataset (only smaller in terms of #subjects, i.e. a total of +-300 subjects out of the +-3000 subjects), it compiles and runs perfectly, and requires about 1GB to 2GB of RAM. The smaller version has about 100 missing values.

If it's only 10 times larger in terms of expression graph
it should only take up 10 times as much space.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Howto compile advanced models?
parts:
Dear Bob, many thanks for your reply. 
I have been working on the model and tweaked some code. The likelihood of my model is as follows, and relates to network meta-analysis:

for (n in 1:N) {
  mu[n] <- alpha[xstudy[n]] + delta[xstudy[n]]*if_else((xtreat[n]-xbaseline[n]), 1, 0); 
  Y[n] ~ multi_normal(mu[n], (S[xstudy[n]]*ar)); //ar is a correlation matrix
}

for (j in 1:Nstudies){
    md[j] <- d[ttreat[j]] - d[tbaseline[j]];
    delta[j] ~ multi_normal(md[j], Sdelta); //Sdelta is a diagonal matrix with a common heterogeneity term
}
Which version of RStan are you using?

I am using RStan 2.6.0. Btw, I discovered that compilation was aborted because the system I am using only allows a certain computation time (it is a high performance system). I changed some settings and now managed to compile the model and retrieve samples from the posterior. Memory requirements remain very high though, for compilation and sampling. The fitted object (with MCMC samples) takes about 2GB. 

I have about 6300 missing values in my data, resulting in 6300 unknown parameters + the standard model parameters (I think about 50). 

In general, results that come out of the model seem to make sense, I just wonder why fitting this model is computationally so exhaustive. The dataset I am working with is of average size (about 2000 subjects), and I hope to apply these methods for larger data sets.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Howto compile advanced models?
parts:
For speed:

1. move to Cholesky factorization of the covariance matrix,

2. compute each study's covariance matrix once and group the
calls to multi_normal by study.

These two steps should provide a substantial speedup.

You also want to replace

if_else(x - y, 1, 0)

with just

(x > y)

in Stan. Similarly for the step() functions. This isn't a big
deal for efficiency, just clarity. But what you really want is to use
conditionals:

mu[n] <- delta[xstudy[n]];
if (x > y)
mu[n] <- mu[n] + 1;

- Bob
